newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra to invest $450 mln in Mexico l-d phones.
newsitem.headline: Alestra to invest $450 mln in Mexico l-d phones.

text.p: Telephone company Alestra will invest $450 million in Mexico in 1997, ready for when the long-distance market is opened to competition on January 1, 1997, the company's CEO told reporters.

"We're over half-way there, and will reach the figure ($450 million) by year's end," Jorge Escalanona, head of Avantel, told a news conference. "We have earmarked $1 billion for investing over the next three years."
Alestra is a joint venture between Mexican industrial giant Alfa and U.S. telephone company AT&T.
Former state-owned company Telefonos de Mexico currently has a monopoly on long distance calls in Mexico, other than those made by cellular telephones.
Escalona estimated that the Mexican market for domestic and international calls is worth $3-4 billion per year.
"We will be competing in a market of $3-4 billion, and in countries where markets have been deregulated, they have grown by up to 20 percent a year," Escalona said.
He added that Mexico is AT&T's biggest market in Latin America. "Calls between Mexico and the U.S. alone top $1 billion. It's the biggest two-way market in the world."

Alestra is within 2,000 km (1,240 miles) of laying its target of 4,300 km (2,670 miles) of fiber optic cables to provide a long distance telephone service in 32 cities across Mexico to begin with, and in 60 cities at a later stage, he added.
